item.title: What you'll see, and what you'll own
item.description: How a Zaions project runs, step by step: writing the brief, the written estimate, milestone links, the packages, the handover and paying an invoice.

item.title: Writing your brief: what to include
item.description: What to put in a Zaions brief, field by field, with an example of a good one. Only your name and email are required; a napkin sketch is a fine start.

item.title: Questions before you hire us, answered
item.description: Short answers about Zaions: who owns the code, what an app costs, how progress is shown, scope changes, maintenance, running costs and where the team is.

item.title: What you own at handover: the checklist
item.description: The code repository and design files move to you at handover, every account ends in your name, and your store listing ships from your own developer account.

item.title: How a project runs, from brief to handover
item.description: Every Zaions project runs in four steps: the brief, a written plan and estimate, a link to the working build at every milestone, then a full handover.

item.title: Open-source cleanup tools for developers
item.description: Three MIT-licensed disk cleanup tools for developers from the Zaions team: windowsweep for Windows, macleanup for macOS and linux-cleanup for Linux.

item.title: Packages explained: which one fits you
item.description: Which Zaions package fits your project, what every package includes, what gets its own estimate, and the running costs your estimate lists beside the price.

item.title: Paying an invoice: the reference to add
item.description: How to pay a Zaions invoice or estimate: pick a method on zaions.com/payments, copy the details, and add the reference from your invoice to the payment note.
